feed.title: NPR Topics: Health
feed.subtitle: Comprehensive health news from NPR. Follow for updates on medical research, wellness trends, public health policy, patient care and healthcare systems.

entry.title: How Sen. Chris Van Hollen plans to flex Democratic power on the foreign aid front
entry.summary: The Maryland Democrat, who's the ranking member of the Senate Foreign Relations Subcommittee, just announced he's going to run for Majority Leader. He spoke to NPR about his foreign aid vision.

entry.title: Happy World Kindness Day! Check out our kind photos of kindness to humans -- and cats
entry.summary: Friday, November 13 is World Kindness Day. Your mission: Do something kind. Small acts of kindness definitely count!

entry.title: Kratom and 7-OH can feel like 'a miracle.' They can also be addictive
entry.summary: In the last decade, strong support for kratom and 7-OH products have kept them federally legal. That's started to change. A crackdown for some highly potent products related to kratom is coming.

entry.title: Fed up with the healthcare industry, this red state capped insulin prices for patients
entry.summary: Republicans and Democrats in North Dakota worked together to limit what people with diabetes have to pay for insulin, joining a growing bipartisan push across the country to protect patients.

entry.title: Ebola tops 11,000 cases in Congo's deadliest outbreak
entry.summary: Congo's Ebola outbreak has topped 11,000 cases, the government said Wednesday, a stark figure that underscores the severity of the situation as the country grapples with the relentless spread of the disease.

entry.title: Seven days of chaos in the ER: How this country's healthcare system is unraveling
entry.summary: Renewed fighting has pushed Ethiopia's healthcare system close to collapse: "The whole emergency (room) was flooded with war trauma patients," one surgeon says of a brutal week in September.

entry.title: Get in, loser: Broadway's newest 'Mean Girls' are ready to insult (and enlighten) you
entry.summary: "School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play," is ending a Broadway run this week and celebrating with livestream broadcasts. We interviewed the Tony-nominated playwright, Jocelyn Bioh.

entry.title: Why honesty is not always the best policy
entry.summary: Should you tell your boss she's got food on her face? Your partner you hate their outfit? Social psychologist Vanessa Bohns shares advice on when to tell someone the truth — or keep your mouth shut.

entry.title: How word of mouth is helping an Amish community's fight against measles
entry.summary: In Pennsylvania, health officials use a quiet vaccination campaign designed to win the trust of the state's Amish community, which has been hit hard by the measles outbreak.

entry.title: How Medicaid affected one California House race
entry.summary: A Republican in California's Central Valley fended off challengers for years. But his district had a lot of people on Medicaid, and he lost by a large margin this time.
